# Cricket Match / Dasha Pattern Analysis (real, computed, exploratory)

**Generated by:** `scripts/build_cricket_match_dasha_dataset.py` (dataset build) +
`scripts/analyze_cricket_match_dasha_patterns.py` (analysis).

**Source data:** user-supplied real ODI match results, 1,053 matches,
2015-01-08 to 2023-08-01 (`Internation Cricket Results.csv`). 806 of 1,053
matches (76.6%) are "eligible" -- both teams map to a real, sourced national
entity in `kundli_mass/nations_corpus.py` (real independence/formation
dates, real capital-city coordinates). 247 matches involving Hong Kong,
Jersey, Scotland, or West Indies were excluded because those are not
single, sourceable sovereign-nation entities under this project's entity
rule.

**Method:** for every eligible match, both teams' national entity chart
(founding-date kundli) was used to compute, AS OF the real match date, the
active Vimshottari Mahadasha lord and Antardasha lord and each lord's
Jyotisha dignity (via this project's existing, unmodified
`world_astrology.reading_engine.build_chart_bundle()` and
`world_astrology.dignity_tables.jyotisha_score()`). This produced 806 rows
of real (not simulated) per-match, per-team dasha/dignity data, saved to
`kundli_mass/cricket_match_dasha_dataset.csv`.

## IMPORTANT: listing-order bias in the source data

Team 1 (as listed in the source CSV) won **476/806 = 59.1%** of matches
overall. This is almost certainly a home/host-country or listing artifact
in the source data, **not** an astrological finding. Because of this, any
comparison must be **listing-order-invariant** (i.e. "did the side with the
higher score win," not "did team1 win when team1 had the higher score") --
otherwise the 59.1% baseline bias contaminates the result. All rates below
are reported in the deconfounded, listing-order-invariant form.

## Findings (real, computed on this 806-match corpus)

| Comparison | n (excl. ties) | Higher-dignity side won | Rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Antardasha-lord Jyotisha score, team vs opponent | 576 | 282 | 49.0% |
| Mahadasha-lord Jyotisha score, team vs opponent | 595 | 320 | 53.8% |

| Own Mahadasha-lord dignity category | n | win rate |
|---|---|---|
| NEUTRAL | 878 | 46.6% |
| N/A (Rahu/Ketu, no classical dignity) | 284 | 55.6% |
| DEBILITATED | 273 | 53.8% |
| OWN_SIGN | 165 | 51.5% |
| EXALTED | 12 | below MIN_SAMPLE_FOR_CLAIM=20, raw counts only (7/12 wins) |

| Own Antardasha-lord dignity category | n | win rate |
|---|---|---|
| NEUTRAL | 863 | 49.5% |
| N/A | 421 | 51.5% |
| DEBILITATED | 162 | 48.1% |
| EXALTED | 101 | 51.5% |
| OWN_SIGN | 65 | 49.2% |

## Honest interpretation

On this univariate, post-hoc, single-feature-at-a-time analysis, **neither
feature shows a strong signal**. Antardasha-lord score comparison is
statistically indistinguishable from a coin flip (49.0%, n=576). Mahadasha
-lord score comparison shows a small effect above 50% (53.8%, n=595), but
this is a modest deviation on a fairly large sample, not a dramatic or
obviously reliable signal, and no significance/confidence-interval test has
been run here.

Per-category win rates for both dasha-lord dignity categories are all
clustered near 46-56%, i.e. close to chance, with no category showing a
large, clearly-separated win rate at adequate sample size.

**This analysis is observational and post-hoc, not a held-out backtest.**
It was run on the entire 806-match corpus with no train/test split, so it
cannot be used to validate a predictive model -- it can only suggest
hypotheses. It should NOT be read as evidence that Vedic dasha/dignity
predicts cricket outcomes, and it is explicitly NOT used to inflate any
`MODEL_CONFIG` weight in `prediction/scorer.py`. Consistent with this
project's standing disclaimer (see `BACKTEST.md`), a real backtest with
proper hindsight protection and out-of-sample evaluation is required before
any claim of predictive validity, and even then a successful backtest would
only demonstrate the performance of this specific implemented algorithm
under its stated assumptions -- not a scientific validation of astrology.

## What this means for the prediction model

Because this exploratory pass did not find a strong single-feature signal,
`prediction/scorer.py`'s `MODEL_CONFIG` weights are NOT derived from this
analysis -- they remain initial, undocumented-as-optimized placeholder
weights (as required by the project spec), and this file's findings are
cited in `BACKTEST.md` as the reason no weight was empirically tuned up
from this dataset. Future work: multi-feature joint models, per-tradition
agreement classification, and true walk-forward backtesting (implemented in
`event_backtest/`) are needed before any weight could be defensibly
adjusted from real evidence.
